prompts.name: summarize_board

arguments.name: board
arguments.description: Board title (or part of it), or a board id

prompts.text:
Summarize the Milanote board "{{board}}".

{{snippet:find_board}}
Then read it with milanote_export_board (the outline keeps columns and notes in order).

Reply with: a two-sentence overview; the main points per column; the open questions and unchecked tasks you found; three suggested next steps. Quote the board's own wording where it matters and do not invent content that is not on the board. Offer to add the next steps to the board as a to-do list (milanote_create_todo_list on the board) — only do it if the user says yes.

prompts.name: organize_board
prompts.title: Organize a board
prompts.description: Propose a tidier structure for a messy board (columns for loose notes), then apply it once the user approves.

arguments.name: board
arguments.description: Board title (or part of it), or a board id

prompts.text:
Help tidy the Milanote board "{{board}}".

{{snippet:find_board}}
Read it with milanote_get_board — you need the element ids.

1. Propose a structure: which columns to create and which existing notes go where (name them by their first line), plus anything that looks like a duplicate. Show this as a short plan and WAIT for the user's approval — move nothing yet.
2. Once approved: create the columns with milanote_create_column, then move each note with milanote_move_element (parentId = the column id). Never trash anything unless the user explicitly asks; if they do, use milanote_trash_element (recoverable from Milanote's trash).
3. Finish with the board link and a list of what changed.

prompts.name: notes_to_tasks
prompts.title: Turn notes into tasks
prompts.description: Extract the concrete actions from a board's notes into a to-do list on that board.

arguments.name: board
arguments.description: Board title (or part of it), or a board id

prompts.text:
Turn the notes on the Milanote board "{{board}}" into a to-do list.

{{snippet:find_board}}
Read it with milanote_export_board.

1. Extract every concrete action (things someone has to do; skip ideas and facts). Write each as a short imperative sentence in the board's own wording; add an owner or deadline only when the board states one. Keep the board's order.
2. Show the list to the user and wait for their confirmation.
3. When confirmed, create it with milanote_create_todo_list (parentId = the board id, title "Action items"), then reply with the board link.

gdd.title: Game design document
gdd.description: A complete GDD: overview, gameplay, content, presentation, technical, production, references.

variables.name: game
variables.description: The game (name, optionally a one-line pitch)

variables.name: platform
variables.description: Target platform / engine (Roblox, Unity, Unreal, web, ...)

gdd.outline:
# {{game}} — Game Design Document
One paragraph on {{game}}: what it is, who it is for and why it will be fun. Platform / engine: {{platform}}.

## 1 · Overview
### Elevator pitch
Two or three sentences that sell the game.
### Design pillars
- **Pillar 1** — one line on what it means for every decision
- **Pillar 2** — …
- **Pillar 3** — …
### Goals & non-goals
**Goals (v1)**
- …
**Non-goals (v1)**
- …
### Audience & platform
- Who plays it, session length, platform / engine ({{platform}}), input methods

## 2 · Gameplay
### Core loop
Title → Play → … → Result → Play again. What pulls the player back in?
### Mechanics
- Mechanic — how it works, why it is fun, how it interacts with the others
### Controls
- Input → action (keyboard / mouse / touch / gamepad)
### Progression & economy
- What the player earns, unlocks and upgrades; how difficulty ramps

## 3 · Content
### Characters
- Playable and non-playable characters, their roles and fantasy
### Levels / world
- Spaces, their purpose, how the player moves between them
### Enemies & challenges
- Threats, puzzles, bosses; what each one teaches

## 4 · Presentation
### Art direction
- Style, palette, references, silhouette rules
### Audio
- Music direction, key sound effects, voice
### UI / UX
- Screen flow, HUD, feedback ("juice"), accessibility

## 5 · Technical
### Architecture
- Modules and how they talk; server vs client; what is pure and testable
### Data & saves
- What persists, where, how it is versioned
### Performance targets
- Frame rate, memory, load times, minimum devices

## 6 · Production
### Milestones
- [ ] M1 — playable core
- [ ] M2 — content complete
- [ ] M3 — polish & release
### Risks
- Risk — likelihood, impact, mitigation
### Open questions
- Question — who decides, by when

## 7 · References
### How to add references
Each reference goes in its own bare ### section as a URL with a short caption — Milanote turns it into a preview card.

character_sheet.outline:
# {{character}} — Character Sheet
Who {{character}} is in one paragraph: role in {{game}}, fantasy, what makes them memorable.

## 1 · Concept
### Identity
- Name, age / origin, one-line description
- Role in the game (playable / boss / ally / vendor)
### Personality
- Three traits and how each shows in animation, dialogue and play
### Backstory
- The two or three beats that matter for the game; leave the rest out

## 2 · Visual design
### Silhouette & colours
- Readable from a distance: shape language, primary / secondary colours
### Outfit & props
- Signature items, what can be customised
### How to add references
Each reference image or page goes in its own bare ### section as a URL — Milanote shows a preview card.

## 3 · Gameplay
### Role & archetype
- Rusher / zoner / grappler / support …; strengths, weaknesses, counters
### Stats
- Health, speed, damage, defence … relative to the roster (low / mid / high)
### Moveset
- [ ] Light attack — description, startup / recovery, damage
- [ ] Heavy attack — …
- [ ] Special 1 — …
- [ ] Special 2 — …
- [ ] Ultimate — …
### Combos & specials
- Bread-and-butter combo, mix-ups, what the player learns first

## 4 · Presentation
### Animations
- [ ] Idle, walk, run, jump
- [ ] One animation per attack
- [ ] Hit reactions, block, KO
- [ ] Victory / taunt
### VFX & SFX
- Signature effects and sounds for each special
### Voice lines
- Intro, taunt, victory, defeat; tone and delivery

## 5 · Production
### Tasks
- [ ] Concept art approved
- [ ] Model & rig
- [ ] Moveset prototyped
- [ ] Balance pass
### Open questions
- Question — who decides

level_design.title: Level design
level_design.description: A level or arena: purpose, layout and flow, encounters, art & audio, blockout tasks and playtest checklist.
level_design.outline:
# {{level}} — Level Design
What {{level}} is for in one paragraph: the fantasy, the player's goal and where it sits in {{game}}.

## 1 · Overview
### Purpose & fantasy
- What the player should feel; what this level teaches or tests
### Setting
- Place, time of day, weather, mood
### Player goals
- Main objective, optional objectives, exit condition

## 2 · Layout
### Zones
- Zone — purpose, size, connections
### Flow & pacing
- Intro → build → peak → release; where the player rests
### Landmarks & navigation
- What is visible from where; how the player never gets lost
### Spawn, camera & bounds
- Spawn points, camera rules, out-of-bounds handling

## 3 · Gameplay
### Encounters
- Encounter — enemies / players, setup, intended solution
### Hazards & interactables
- Traps, moving parts, breakables, pickups
### Difficulty curve
- How challenge ramps inside the level and compared with the previous one

## 4 · Art & audio
### Palette & lighting
- Colours, key light, fog / post effects
### Props
- [ ] Hero props (unique)
- [ ] Set dressing (kit)
- [ ] Skybox / backdrop
### Ambience & music
- Loops, stingers, spatial sounds

## 5 · Production
### Blockout tasks
- [ ] Greybox layout
- [ ] Playable path
- [ ] Encounter pass
- [ ] Art pass
- [ ] Polish & optimisation
### Playtest checklist
- [ ] A new player finds the objective within 30 seconds
- [ ] No dead ends without a reward
- [ ] Frame rate holds on the minimum device
### Open questions
- Question — who decides

snippets.workflow:
Work like this:
1. Call milanote_whoami first. If it reports "Not signed in", call milanote_login, ask the user to sign in in the window that opens, then retry. Look at `usage`: if the free-plan headroom is too small for what you are about to build, say so before building.
2. Write the WHOLE board as one Markdown outline in the Milanote++ outline format and create it with ONE milanote_build_board call. Build it inside the user's Home board unless they named another board (find ids with milanote_list_boards or milanote_search). Fill every section with specific content for this case — no placeholders, no "TBD", no template wording left behind; drop sections that do not apply and add ones that do. Keep each note under about 120 words and prefer bullets.
3. Reply with the board link (the `url` the tool returns), a short summary of the key points, and one question about what to go deeper on.
snippets.outline_format: Outline format reminder: `# Title` creates the sub-board (plain text right under it becomes the title note); `## Column` starts a column; `### Heading` starts a note that runs until the next ### / ##; a ### section whose lines are all `- [ ] task` becomes a to-do list; a bare `###` followed by a URL (plus optional caption) becomes a link card. Notes accept light Markdown (bullets, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, > quotes).
snippets.find_board: Find the board first: call milanote_whoami, then, if the name looks like a 14-character id, use it directly; otherwise call milanote_list_boards (depth 4) and pick the best title match — if several boards match, ask which one before doing anything.
